checks.command: jq -e '.key_a == 26 and .key_b == 87 and .steps == 64 and .first_retinal_transition_a == 1 and .first_retinal_transition_b == 1 and .first_learner_divergence == 1 and .first_candidate_divergence == 1 and .first_choice_divergence == 1 and .first_movement_divergence == 1' research/campaigns/workstation-return-bearing-opportunity-composition-v1/artifacts/threshold-retinotopic-visual-transition-64.json

findings: The 26/87 real-key pair first diverges in admitted retina, actual learner state, candidate evaluation, resolved choice, and physical movement at sequence 1 in both the focused and held-out traces.
Removing visual outcome return, signed retinotopy, or ordinal threshold factorization independently removes the choice and movement divergence.
The retained impulse-magnitude arm changes actual learner state but never reaches a different candidate through 64 steps, confirming that a receptor threshold absorbs scalar impulse magnitude.
The dedicated learner fingerprint excludes workstation and retinal adapter state, so diagnostic divergence now names the core learner rather than the whole checkpoint.

The accepted hand trajectory, legacy and current checkpoint replay, passive-world-change rejection, natural quiescence, semantic firewall, formatting, compilation, clippy, and warm regression budget remain intact.
residual_uncertainty: This supports cue-dependent visual motor choice only; neither run presses its illuminated key, so it does not establish visual reaching, intended key selection, gaze centering, or hand-eye coordination.
The result uses one workstation morphology and one opposite real-key pair; transfer to other cue locations, binocular disparities, presentations, and morphologies remains untested.
Threshold factorization is research-only and has not passed a frozen authority protocol.
